LSU Tigers.previous_hc_experience: Extensive. The guide records a collective 32-6 run over his final three seasons at Ole Miss, and raises his earlier USC spell as the cautionary comparison.
LSU Tigers.oc: Charlie Weis Jr., brought from Ole Miss — the Ole Miss spread (p. 305) describes him as central to that offense and records him going to Baton Rouge.
LSU Tigers.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
LSU Tigers.dc_status: Returning — Baker enters his third season, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
LSU Tigers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The Coaching Carousel says Kiffin plays an exciting style of football.
LSU Tigers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
LSU Tigers.qb_development: Not addressed as a development record. The guide reports Kiffin told ESPN his concern about Sam Leavitt was the transition into the offense rather than his health.
LSU Tigers.continuity: Split. The head coach and offensive coordinator are both new but arrive together from Ole Miss, while Blake Baker returns for a third season on defense.
LSU Tigers.staff_turnover: The guide's framing is that Kiffin brought key staff from Ole Miss rather than rebuilding, so the change is a transplant rather than a teardown.
LSU Tigers.prior_school: Ole Miss, extensively — Kiffin, coordinator Charlie Weis Jr., five-star defensive end Princewill Umanmielen (51 pressures and 11 sacks there) and TJ Dottery, who tied for the sixth-most tackles in the SEC.
LSU Tigers.portal_recruiting: Kiffin took 41 portal commits, sixth-most nationally, which the guide calls the best transfer class in the country; per Phil Steele it brought 107 career starts. Entire position groups are being rebuilt, including nine receiver transfers and five more defensive linemen.
LSU Tigers.vsin_assessment: Admiring but watchful. The Coaching Carousel calls Kiffin one of the most recognizable cast members in the college football soap opera, credits recruiting at an obscene level and the 32-6 finish at Ole Miss, and asks directly whether the LSU move conjures memories of his ill-fated USC stint — answering probably, given the blue blood in both institutions — before concluding that he plays an exciting style and gets players who can ball out on both sides, which is just what LSU needs. The team page rates him an elite coach for whom success on the biggest stage has been elusive.
LSU Tigers.strengths: Elite recruiting and portal work, a proven late-tenure record at his previous stop, resources the guide says LSU has provided, and a retained defensive coordinator the guide credits with transforming the unit.
LSU Tigers.concerns: The USC precedent, and the practical risk of rebuilding entire position groups at once — the guide notes others have been burned building the plane while flying it.
LSU Tigers.betting: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins. The coaching change is not the stated reason: the guide allows the transfer class might be enough to lift Kiffin to the top of the SEC, and blames a hard schedule and a quarterback returning from a serious foot injury. It notes Kiffin's $91 million contract drew the headlines while pointing to the more than $3 million a year paid to Baker.
LSU Tigers.carousel_summary: The guide treats the move as an event in itself, noting Kiffin bailed on a College Football Playoff squad to set things in motion at LSU, and flags September 19 — LSU at Ole Miss — as possibly the season's must-see game. It balances the theatre against the record: he recruited at an obscene level and led a 32-6 run over his final three seasons with the Rebels. Its stated question is whether the move recalls his ill-fated USC stint, and its answer is probably, given the blue blood running through both institutions. It closes on what is not arguable — Kiffin plays an exciting style and gets players who can ball out on both sides, which it calls just what LSU needs.

Mississippi State Bulldogs.dc: Zach Arnett, brought back as coordinator.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.dc_status: New — the guide records Lebby addressing the defense by bringing back Zach Arnett as coordinator, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide's stated plan is Lebby building an offense around KaMario Taylor's explosive running ability.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated tendency. The guide records the 2025 run game as average at 3.7 yards per carry and 158 yards per game, and expects improvement with a dual-threat quarterback.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide expects Taylor's explosiveness to unlock more for Lebby's offense.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.continuity: Partial. Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback both change.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive side, where Lebby brought Zach Arnett back.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.portal_recruiting: Not addressed in guide as a staff-driven effect.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.vsin_assessment: Pointed. The guide frames year three as make-or-break, noting Lebby is still seeking a second SEC win as head coach and is 1-15 straight up in conference play. It is careful to add he is 9-7 against the spread in those games, so he beats market expectations even while losing, then is blunt that he needs actual wins to keep his job.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.strengths: Offensive continuity at coordinator, year-to-year improvement from two wins to five, and a market record that outperforms the results.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.concerns: A 1-15 SEC record, a defense that allowed 30.4 points per game, and a schedule on which the guide says any SEC wins would come as major upsets.
Mississippi State Bulldogs.betting: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins. The coaching link is explicit in both directions: the bull case is Lebby building around Taylor's explosiveness, and the requirement is that Arnett improve a defense that allowed 30.4 points per game. The guide also notes Lebby's 9-7 ATS record in SEC games as evidence he beats market expectations while losing.

Missouri Tigers.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Missouri Tigers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Missouri Tigers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated tendency, though the guide expects the rushing attack to remain the offense's backbone and asks whether it is the best in the country.
Missouri Tigers.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback both change.
Missouri Tigers.portal_recruiting: Austin Simmons arrives from Ole Miss; the guide asks whether he could be the steal of the transfer portal.
Missouri Tigers.vsin_assessment: Positive on the base, impatient for the next step. The guide frames Missouri as quietly consistent under Eliah Drinkwitz, says the foundation is built and the next step is overdue, and records that over the last three seasons the Tigers are 29-10 straight up, 15-9 in the SEC and 25-14 against the spread. What is missing is an SEC Championship or playoff appearance, and it is candid that this is a hard year to get one.
Missouri Tigers.strengths: Sustained results — 29-10 over three seasons with a positive market record — plus nine returning offensive starters and 30-plus points per game in two of the last three seasons.
Missouri Tigers.concerns: No SEC Championship or playoff appearance, a defense the guide calls suspect with only three starters back, and a conference in which few contenders can be displaced.
Missouri Tigers.betting: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins. The guide finds it hard to believe an offense of this caliber wins six or fewer, conditional on Austin Simmons cutting out mistakes, and argues few of Missouri's rivals match its offensive potential.
Missouri Tigers.conflicts: The team page (p. 300) prints total 12 returning starters with offense 9 and defense 6; offense plus defense is 15, which does not equal the printed total. All three figures are reproduced as printed and none is corrected.

Oklahoma Sooners.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Oklahoma Sooners.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Oklahoma Sooners.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name, though the guide says better play-calling is needed on the ground alongside the new offensive linemen.
Oklahoma Sooners.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide records the unit finished third in defensive efficiency by EPA and led the country in success rate.
Oklahoma Sooners.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated tendency. The guide records a team-wide rushing failure — 3.5 yards per carry, 127th in rushing EPA per play and 128th in success rate — that coordinator Ben Arbuckle has to fix.
Oklahoma Sooners.qb_development: Not addressed as a record, but a pre-existing relationship is central: Arbuckle was John Mateer's coordinator at Washington State, and the guide benchmarks Mateer's Oklahoma season against his form there.
Oklahoma Sooners.continuity: Complete. Head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback all return, for a Stability Score of 17.
Oklahoma Sooners.prior_school: Washington State, where Arbuckle coached Mateer before both arrived at Oklahoma.
Oklahoma Sooners.portal_recruiting: Not addressed in guide as a staff-driven effect.
Oklahoma Sooners.vsin_assessment: The guide describes Brent Venables as consistently inconsistent — two 10-win seasons and two 6-7 seasons in Norman, with 2025 producing a fifth playoff appearance.
Oklahoma Sooners.strengths: Total continuity, an elite defense the guide expects to repeat, and a coordinator who already knows the quarterback from a more productive season together.
Oklahoma Sooners.concerns: The head coach's alternating record, and an offense that failed on the ground badly enough that the guide says play-calling must improve as well as personnel.
Oklahoma Sooners.betting: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins. The guide's logic runs through the coaching split: if the defense is close to its 2025 level — which it expects — the win floor is very high, leaving the offense as the open question.

Ole Miss Rebels.previous_hc_experience: None as a head coach beyond the interim spell the guide describes — Golding is a first-time head coach charged with sustaining what he achieved on an interim basis.
Ole Miss Rebels.oc: John David Baker, East Carolina's coordinator in 2025.
Ole Miss Rebels.oc_status: New — Baker replaces Charlie Weis Jr., and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Ole Miss Rebels.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Ole Miss Rebels.play_caller: Changed, and the guide treats it as material: Golding had Weis calling plays in the postseason and now does not.
Ole Miss Rebels.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide flags the practical consequences of the change as new terminology and unknown play structure and flow.
Ole Miss Rebels.continuity: Broken where it mattered most. The quarterback and defensive coordinator return, but the head coach is new in a permanent capacity and the offensive coordinator who ran the unit has left.
Ole Miss Rebels.staff_turnover: Golding replaced his offensive staff and retooled the skill positions; the guide notes he has had to hire a coordinator, rebuild groups such as receiver, and take charge of every facet.
Ole Miss Rebels.prior_school: The Coaching Carousel lists Golding's lineage: Todd Monken at Southern Miss, Ron Roberts at SE Louisiana, Frank Wilson at UTSA, Nick Saban at Alabama, and Kiffin. Coordinator John David Baker comes from East Carolina.
Ole Miss Rebels.portal_recruiting: Not addressed as a staff-driven effect beyond the retooled skill positions.
Ole Miss Rebels.vsin_assessment: Doubtful, and stated plainly. The guide poses the question directly — does Golding have head-coaching ability, or did he benefit from inheriting Lane Kiffin's team mid-run — and states its doubt about him openly. The Coaching Carousel is sympathetic to the athletic director's position while calling it hard not to feel underwhelmed, given Kiffin's offensive reputation and recruiting, though it credits the Rebels for playing extremely well in the CFP, beating Tulane and Georgia before falling short to Miami.
Ole Miss Rebels.strengths: Player buy-in — the Coaching Carousel notes the players rallied around Golding amid the drama of Kiffin's exit — a broad coaching lineage, and a genuine CFP run under him.
Ole Miss Rebels.concerns: A first-time head coach steering a programme with national title ambitions through a brutal conference, without the play-caller who ran the postseason offense. As a defensive coach, the guide expects his coordinator choice to hang over the season if the offense starts slowly.
Ole Miss Rebels.betting: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins, argued directly from coaching: the departures of the architects of one of the country's better offenses matter more than 16 returning starters, and combined with a taxing schedule the guide says it could mean a disappointing season in Oxford.
Ole Miss Rebels.carousel_summary: The guide frames this as a tough situation for AD Keith Carter: the players rallied around Golding amid the made-for-TV drama of Kiffin's exit, yet set against Kiffin's offensive reputation and recruiting — including in the JUCO ranks — it says it is hard not to feel underwhelmed. It gives the counterweight fairly, noting the Rebels played extremely well in the CFP, beating Tulane and Georgia before falling short to Miami. It closes by listing the coaches Golding has worked under: Todd Monken at Southern Miss, Ron Roberts at SE Louisiana, Frank Wilson at UTSA, Nick Saban at Alabama, and Kiffin.
